President Trump is defending his remarks
after he called Russian leader Vladimir Putin a friend,
but Trump said he can't speak to whether
Putin is a friend to the U.S.
NPR White House correspondent Franco Ordonez
has more on the president's wide-ranging news conference
Friday after returning from China with meetings with Putin
and China's President Xi Jinping.
I mean, Trump was asked today of Putin,
who he called his friend, was also America's friend.
You know, he really couldn't answer that,
but he did continue to make the case
that his relationship with Putin
would reap benefits for America,
though we haven't really seen that yet.
You know, the war in Ukraine continues to rage on,
but we are seeing allies start to build alliances
with other nations as, you know,
confidence in the U.S. falters,
and they look to reduce their dependence on the U.S.
In an interview with the BBC,
Ukraine's President Vladimir Zelensky
responded to Trump's remark,
and he said to the people of Ukraine,
"Putin is an enemy for us.
He's a killer."
The Senate passed its first bill on prediction markets
that would ban bets tied to "Death and War,"
NPR's Luke Garrett reports.
Democratic Senator Adam Schiff of California
and Republican Senator John Curtis of Utah
wrote the bill that passed the Senate
by voice vote on Thursday.
Schiff has been critical of prediction market regulator
the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
In the absence of real leadership and enforcement
at the CFTC, it's time for Congress to step in
and fix this problem.
With our bill, Congress is making clear
that these bets should be illegal once and for all.
The CFTC already restricts bets connected to war
and terrorism on U.S.-regulated prediction markets,
but the Senate bill would broaden and strengthen a ban
on trades tied to a person's death.
The bill now goes to the House.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
A new study shows six in 10 people
who used AI for health advice say they would believe
a chatbot, even if it contradicted
their healthcare provider, NPR's Windsor Johnston reports.
Talker Research conducted the survey
for the virtual care company MD Live.
Medical director Dr. Maggie Williams says chatbots
give quick, confident answers at any hour.
By the time patients come in, she says,
many have already asked a chatbot about their symptoms.
That happens every day, multiple times a day,
and I think, honestly, many of our patients
have conferred with CLOD or another resource
and maybe don't even disclose it.
Williams says the risk goes both ways.
A chatbot could get someone to the ER sooner,
but it can also suggest breathing exercises
for chest pressure when someone's having a heart attack.
Windsor Johnston, NPR News.
On Wall Street, all three indexes finished sharply lower
on Friday. You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
With the 3 a.m. Eastern Time deadline now having passed,
Union security watchmen who guard the giant ports
at Los Angeles and Long Beach could be on strike Saturday.
The guards are represented by the International Longshore
and Warehouse Union.
They have been negotiating with management
for more than a year.
A walkout could disrupt cargo at the nation's busiest
port complex during the key holiday shopping season.
Colorado has declared its second major disaster this month
after heavy flooding from member station KSUT,
Adam Burke reports.
Repeated flooding in the Four Corners region
destroyed roads, bridges, and critical infrastructure
and displaced thousands of residents.
In its formal request to the White House,
Colorado put preliminary reconstruction cost estimates
for public infrastructure at $28.5 million.
The state expects those numbers to increase.
Governor Jared Polis says the Trump administration
has not responded to the state's first $27 million request
delivered on October 31st.
We hope that nobody plays politics with the lives
of real people, many of whom lost their homes.
Flooding impacted New Mexico, Arizona, Utah,
and tribal nations as well.
Recovery cost estimates have grown to the hundreds
of millions of dollars.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Burke in Durango.
The latest version of Grand Theft Auto VI
is a big hit with gamers, Rockstar Games,
which developed the game,
said the new version generated a record,
nearly $3.8 billion in sales in the first day.
I'm Dan Ronan, NPR News, Washington.
